habitat: Singly or in pairs in savanna and woodland.
summary: A black stork with a white belly and rump. Newman’s description gives the habitat and little else, and it does not say whether Kruger birds are resident or visitors. No month list was stored.

similar.note: Black Stork is larger, with a red bill and red legs, and a black rump in flight. Abdim’s Stork has a white rump.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Black stork with a white belly, in savanna or woodland.
Black head. The bill colour was not named.
White rump. A separate upperwing pattern was not named.

calls.description: No call was described, and no usable recording was found.

research.note: Status and months were left unset. Newman does not say resident or visitor, only that it occurs in savanna and woodland. The only playable recording found was grade D wingbeats, so no call was stored. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.
